title: Phased Integration - Cache Occupancy Profiling and Fleet Impact
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures profiling and capacity-impact analysis for a planned phased integration of a new generation decoder model (gen-2-small) across regions. Focus is on expected KV cache occupancy, downstream GPU slot pressure, and suggested stagger/warmup levers to avoid eviction storms and latency SLO violations.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Preliminary sims indicate gen-2-small increases median per-request KV footprint by ~38% vs current baseline (gen-1-medium) for our chat traffic mix, driven by longer average prompt context and more system tokens. If deployed uniformly, expected steady-state KV occupancy rises by ~22% in us-west1 and ~17% in eu-west1, translating to 8-12% additional GPU slot pressure under current admission controls. A phased rollout with region-first warmup, seeded traffic, and adaptive admission thresholds can keep end-to-end latency within SLO while limiting slot adds to targeted bursts rather than permanent fleet expansion.

Assumptions and definitions:
- Model: gen-2-small (decoder-only, 25B-ish params equivalent); baseline: gen-1-medium.
- Prefix distribution: 45% short (<128 tokens), 40% medium (128-512), 15% long (>512).
- Avg KV entry size per token (quantized): 12 bytes (post-4bit/8bit quantization heuristics).
- KV TTL semantics: hot prefixes retained for 6 minutes by default, LRU eviction after capacity threshold.
- Admission controls: soft-slot threshold 85% (pressure alarms), hard threshold 98% (request reject/fallback).
- Warmup means seeding requests to pre-populate KV caches on warm nodes before full rollout.
- Sim horizon: first 14 days of rollout, with day-0 heavy traffic (canary ingress) and day 3/7 ramps.

Workload profiles used in simulation:
- Prod-chat: conservative 60% of rollout traffic (mixed user sessions, high KV reuse).
- Assist-bots: 25% (higher context carryover, higher KV churn).
- Search-embeds: 15% (negligible KV use).
- Region weight: us-west1 52%, eu-west1 36%, ap-southeast1 12% (traffic routed by region-locality).

Key metrics computed (per region):
- Steady-state KV occupancy (GB) = sum_over_prefixes(avg_KV_per_request * qps * hot_fraction * avg_ttl)
- GPU slot pressure = (effective_qps_per_model / slot_throughput) adjusted for batching and cache hits
- Eviction rate (entries/sec) triggered by cache shortfall

Profiling results (simulation snapshot):
- us-west1 (baseline gen-1-medium):
  - Baseline KV occupancy: 1,240 GB
  - Predicted gen-2-small occupancy: 1,520 GB (+280 GB, +22.6%)
  - Baseline effective slots used: 420 slots avg
  - Predicted slots: 460 slots avg (+40 slots, +9.5%)
  - Eviction bursts predicted during warmup spikes: up to 18k evictions/minute if no seed traffic

- eu-west1:
  - Baseline KV occupancy: 860 GB
  - Predicted occupancy: 1,008 GB (+148 GB, +17.2%)
  - Baseline slots: 290
  - Predicted slots: 316 (+26, +9.0%)
  - Eviction bursts: up to 11k evictions/minute in unseeded ramp

- ap-southeast1 (small region):
  - Baseline occupancy: 300 GB
  - Predicted occupancy: 360 GB (+60 GB, +20%)
  - Slots: 110 -> 118 (+8)
  - Risk: higher P95 latency drift due to thin eviction margins

Observed drivers of increase:
1) Longer average generated tokens per request (system behaviors and default prompt templates).
2) Larger per-token KV footprint due to model parameterization and quantization inefficiencies for longer sequences.
3) Lower reuse ratios for assist-bots workload because of session variation.

Warmup & staged rollout strategy (recommended):
- Phase A: Canary (us-west1) 0.5% traffic for 24 hours with heavy synthetic seed traffic to pre-populate KV. Monitor eviction rate and P95 latency.
- Phase B: Warm lane expansion (us-west1 + eu-west1) 5% traffic for 48 hours. Increase seed proportion to 30% of actual canary qps.
- Phase C: Regional increment (ap-southeast1) limited to 2% with dedicated seed for 72 hours because of narrow headroom.
- Phase D: Gradual global roll to 25% over 7 days with dynamic autoscale policies triggered at 80% soft thresholds.
- Full flip contingent on day-7 quality metrics: P95 latency within +10% of baseline, eviction rate < threshold, no degrade in error rate.

Mitigation levers (ordered by low-to-high cost):
- Prompt-level: trim default system tokens for long sessions; shorter instruction templates. (low effort)
- Runtime: increase KV hot TTL from 6min -> 9min for seeded warm nodes (reduces churn during ramp). (config change)
- Admission: temporarily raise soft threshold to 90% with higher priority routing for canary traffic. (medium risk)
- Caching: enable prefix-level dedupe heuristics for high-similarity requests to cut duplicate KV entries (~12% reduction in occupancy in sim). (engineering work)
- Fleet: enable burst-only reserved slots in us-west1 (add 40 slots in burst pool) to handle warmup spike; evaluate permanent capacity add if sustained for >14 days. (higher cost)

Failure scenarios & safeguards:
- Eviction storm: if eviction rate exceeds 25k/min sustained for >10min, automatic rollback to gen-1-medium and creation of incident ticket.
- Latency SLO breach: if P95 > baseline + 20% for 30min, throttle rollout to previous phase and increase seed ratio.
- Autoscale lag: if GPU slot request latency > 2x baseline during warmup, trigger pre-warm script to spin spare nodes in warm mode.

Sensitivity table (summary):
- KV per-token delta +-10% -> occupancy change +-8-10%
- Hot TTL +-2min -> eviction rate changes up to +-18% during ramp
- Seed ratio (0% -> 30%) -> reduces eviction spikes by ~65% in sim

Operational playbook checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Create canary traffic generator config and run in staging (owner: Aaron Li, due: 2025-11-12)
- [ ] Update runtime TTL override API for warm nodes (owner: Mateo Ruiz, due: 2025-11-14)
- [ ] Instrument eviction telemetry with per-region alert (owner: Janelle Park, due: 2025-11-10)
- [ ] Add rollout gate to CI/CD pipeline referencing INFRA-2741 (owner: Priya Khatri, due: 2025-11-18)
- [ ] Draft rollback runbook and automated rollback job in K8s operator (owner: SRE, due: 2025-11-20)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can model quantization be optimized specifically for KV layouts to reduce per-token bytes? (Research + Applied ML)
- Will customers with long-session configs be prioritized separately during rollout? (Product decision)
- Should we provision a temporary regional cache tier (RAM-only) to reduce eviction churn during first 72 hours? Cost estimate required.

Appendix A - quick simulation notes:
- Simulator uses 1-minute timestep, LRU eviction policy approximation, and per-prefix hot fraction heuristics sampled from production trace (Sept-Nov 2025).
- Batching assumptions: avg batch size 6 requests during normal steady-state; reduces to 3 during warmup due to traffic fragmentation.
- Validation: ran 50 Monte Carlo sims with seed traffic scaling 0-40% to compute percentile ranges in table above.

Appendix B - quick links to artifacts and dashboards:
- Dashboards: /d/kv-occupancy/us-west1 (internal)
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/rollout-runbook-gen2
- Jira: INFRA-2741 (onboarding plan), INFRA-2750 (eviction-alerts)
